newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express

CONGRESS PARTY CHIEF BACKTRACKS Congress chief Sitaram Kesri did a complete turn around and said he was ready for a formal dialogue with the United Front. Kesri was busy consulting senior colleagues and members of the working committee to work out the modalities for the talks.
This change in attitude came hours after several Congress leaders and MPs mounted pressure to form a committee to open formal dialogue with the Front and avert the likelihood of mid term polls.
The Times Of India
HIGH COURT FREES POLITICAL BIGWIGS FROM SCAM SHACKLES

The Delhi High Court set aside the order of a special judge and quashed the hawala (money laundering) proceedings against Bharatiya Janata Party president LK Advani and former minister VC Shukla, among others.

The court ruled that there was no evidence against the petitioners which could be converted into legal evidence. The government was studying the judgment to explore the scope for challenging it in the apex court, sources said.
The Economic Times
GOVERNMENT OFFERS OLIVE BRANCH TO STRIKING TRUCKERS

A breakthrough was reached between the government and the striking truckers with the government proposing to collect service tax from the consignor or the consignee instead of the truck operator. Industry chambers, informed of the new proposal, agreed to collect the taxes on behalf of the government.

So far there was no decision to call off the strike and truckers said it would continue indefinitely. The truck operators were not hopeful of a breakthrough on the insurance premia issue at the proposed meeting with the Parliamentary Standing Committee attached to the finance ministry.
CORPORATES GRIPE ABOUT HUGE STOCK PILE-UP

As the country wide truckers' strike entered its second week, corporates started complaining about huge inventory pile ups. Among the worst hit were soft drinks major Pepsi, car manufacturer Daewoo and cigarette maker Godfrey Phillips.

There was also a halt in the despatch of April stocks from sugar mills across the country. Escorts, which cut motorcycle production by a third, said assembly of two wheelers might be suspended altogether if the strike continued for another week.
Ispat Industries was planning to cut back sponge iron production by 30 percent in the next couple of days.
GE SHELVES PLAN TO ACQUIRE ITC CLASSIC

GE Capital decided to withdraw from the race to acquire ITC Classic. The exercise carried out by the US company failed to yield results largely owing to the stiff non-performing assets (NPA) noms insisted upon by them. GE insisted that an asset be construed as non-performing if outstandings against it went beyond a period of three months.
Going by the GE formula, which was even stricter than the central bank's norms currently in force, ITC Classic would have had to declare almost 90 percent of its assets as NPAs.
HYUNDAI HEADS RACE FOR PRIZED IPS POWER ORDER

Hyundai Engineering of South Korea was expected to bag the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract for IPS Power Company's 3.5 billion rupee naphtha-based combined cycle power project coming up in Karnataka.
Bechtel Corporation and Larsen & Toubro were also in the running for the prized deal. IPS Power is the wholly-owned subsidiary of Boston-based Thermo Ecotek, part of the Thermo Electron Corporation.
The EPC contract was finalised by project promoters, Thermo Ecotek, in consultation with the Karnataka Electricity Board.
Financial Express
BANKERS FOR HIKING CAP ON EQUITY INVESTMENTS
The central bank (RBI) was under pressure to raise the cap on banks' investments in the equity market, currently pegged at five percent of the incremental deposits of the previous year.

Senior bankers felt the RBI in its monetary policy for the first half of 1997/98 April-March) might raise the present ceiling on a selective basis. This, in effect, would raise banks' investments in the secondary market.

The RBI had allowed banks to invest in the secondary market when it announced the busy season credit policy in October 1996. Bankers felt the five percent cap should be raised to ensure investments in the secondary market.
STATE BANK MOVES LAW MINISTRY ON CREDIT PANEL

The State Bank of India (SBI) moved the law ministry to activate the central office credit committee to expedite the credit delivery system. The committee empowered to sanction all mega credit proposals worth up to two billion rupees had not been able to function, pending the approval from the central bank which holds the majority stake in SBI.
The SBI Act does not provide for delegation of board powers to the executives. The committee would have the power to sanction up to two billion rupees inclusive of non fund exposure.
RELIANCE TO CHALLENGE ADDITIONAL CUSTOMS LEVY

Customs authorities slapped an additional 401.5 million rupee import duty on Reliance Industries (RIL) for alleged irregularities in imports of a purified terephthalic acid (PTA) plant in Maharashtra.
The company imported the PTA plant at a cost of over 650 million rupees and had paid customs duty to the tune of an equivalent amount before the case was booked against it.

A Reliance spokesman said the company would challenge a part of the order where the value of the plant was notionally enhanced to arrive at the deemed value. The case against the company was registered in 1988.
COS GIVES GO-AHEAD TO ADVANCE QR PHASE-OUT PLAN
The government was considering phasing out quantative restrictions (QRs) on imports to three years instead of the earlier approved five years.

The revised phase-out plan recommended removing all restrictions on imports of agricultural products by 1999/2OO0, against the earlier move to keep them out of the purview of negotiations with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) committee on balance of payment restrictions.

The Committee of Secretaries (CoS) ratified the commerce ministry's proposals to remove all QRs by April 1, 2000. The CoS decision was forwarded to the cabinet for approval before talks with the WTO resumed in June.
Business Standard
IBM PLANS 100 PCT SUBSIDIARY IN INDIA

IBM Corp has plans to set up a 100 percent subsidiary in India in six months. The company, however, declined to reveal the size of the investment planned for the subsidiary. IBM already has a presence in India through its joint venture with Tata Information Systems.
IBM World Trade holds a 50 percent stake in Tata Information Systems. An IBM official said its move to set up its subsidiary would not affect its association with the Tatas.

However, Tata Sons, the holding company for all Tata firms, ruled out the possibility of IBM setting up a wholly owned subsidiary and said they would have a stake in it if IBM decided to set up a separate company .
ONGC SECURES $160 MLN FROM FOREIGN EXCHANGE DEPOSITS

The Oil and Natural Gas Commission (ONGC) had secured a $160 million loan from the foreign currency non-resident deposits of a consortium of domestic banks at a marginally lower rate of interest than the cost of external commercial borrowings.
The loan was raised at 100 basis points above the ruling London inter-bank offer rate of 5.6 percent against 7 percent in the case of external commercial borrowings.
CALCUTTA BOURSE RESTRUCTURES INDEX BASE YEAR

The Calcutta bourse (CSE) overhauled its index from April 4, 1997. The new index was based on 50 scrips as opposed to the 51 scrips that constituted the earlier index. The base year of the new index was changed from 1987 to 1996. CSE authorities said the index was revamped to make it more representative of present market trends and reflect true market sentiments.
NON BANKING FINANCE COMPANIES LINE UP FOR INSURANCE FORAYS
Leading non-banking finance companies (NBFC) planned to enter the insurance sector even though the budget has only freed up the health insurance segment to date.

Insurance products were being perceived as being meant for savings making it an attractive retailing proposition in coming years. NBFCs, with retail finance as their core competency, were looking at various areas. These included life, health and other specialised products ranging from truck insurance to asset protection, along with risk management products and services.
US ENVOY URGED TO PRESSURE RAYTHEON TO SPEED UP PROJECT
The civil aviation ministry requested the US ambassador to pressure Raytheon to speed up the testing of equipment installed by it at the Delhi air traffic control tower.
The minister reportedly told the ambassador that in spite of extending the deadline several times, Raytheon was yet to make any headway in making the equipment operational.

The Airport Authority of India had even decided to invoke the penalty clause against Raytheon for failing to keep the deadline for carrying out system site acceptance tests on the equipment. But it later refrained from taking action following another request from Raytheon to extend the deadline till April.
49 PCT PRIVATE PLACEMENT IN BPL CELLULAR
BPL was privately placing 49 percent of the equity of BPL Cellular Holdings with Peregrine-led Asia Infrastructure Fund and US insurance giant American International Group.

Analysts estimated the deal to be worth about $200 million. The private placement comes barely six months after BPL Cellular's aborted American depository receipts issue in October 1996 and was seen as an attempt to bridge the funds gap caused by the issue's withdrawal.
The Observer of Business and Politics
FOREIGN INVESTMENTS SHY AWAY AFTER NO TO TATA-SIA

Karnataka, once seen as India's gateway for Singapore's economic regionalisation drive, is witnessing a waning interest after the rejection of the Tata-Singapore airline joint venture proposal. Second guesses on the terms of the proposed Bangalore international airport and aggressive wooing by Tamil Nadu also contributed to Karnataka losing its attraction.

A Singapore business delegation would go to Madras, the capital of Tamil Nadu, to sign an agreement to set up a One-Stop Window for Singaporean investments there. Observers and business sources said the initiatives may lead to a second investment wind for Tamil Nadu from Singapore.
Business Line
MINISTRY SETS 24-HOUR DEADLINE FOR TRUCKERS
The surface transport ministry decided to recommend revocation of transporters' operating permits if the nationwide strike was not called off within 24 hours.

The proposal to take on the truck operators head-on instead of buckling to their demands came in the wake of a deadlock on the eighth day of the strike. Top Ministry officials said the authorities would have no choice but to act and prevent the economy from coming to a standstill, since the truckers refused to reach a settlement.

While the movement of essential commodities and petroleum was resumed in some states, intra-state transport continued to be disrupted by the strike. Industrial production had also started reeling under its impact.
